items.statement: Order book stands at INR165 crores, with INR105 crores from technology solutions and INR60 crores from water resource management
items.quote: Our order book now stands at a healthy INR165 crores, supported by new wins in BFSI healthcare and manufacturing. In that INR165 crores, INR105 crores come from technology solutions vertical.

items.statement: Fortira order book is close to $15 million for current year, adding substantially to consolidated order book
items.quote: Fortira also, this year order book is close to 15 million again there and we have the 51% on that. So there is a substantial addition to the order book what we have on the standalone.

items.statement: Total income for FY25 stood at INR90.6 crores, reflecting 19% year-on-year growth
items.quote: Total income for FY25 stood at INR90.6 crores, reflecting 19% year -on-year growth, led by strong momentum in technology solution, which grew 24% year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA stood at INR14.1 crores with 15.5% margin, a marginal dip due to strategic investments and market conditions
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR14.1 crores, with 15.5% margin. There's a slight dip, you might have noticed. Marginal dip.

items.statement: PAT margin was 9.2% at INR8.3 crores, maintaining profitability while investing for growth
items.quote: The profit margins, that is the profit after tax, stood at INR8.3 crores, with a pet margin of 9.2%, showing that we maintained profitability, even while investing for growth.

items.statement: IT solutions margins typically 22-25%, water resource management similar but working capital requirements dip margins
items.quote: So typically, the margins on the IT solution side are around 22% to 25%. And in water resource also, it is on the little similar lines.

items.statement: IPO proceeds mostly utilized except INR5 crores remaining for solution development
items.quote: No, I think most of the objects have been used except for the solution development object. That's around INR5 crores available and apart from that, we have utilized the other money in the other objects.

items.statement: Acquired 51% stake in Fortira Inc for USD2.55 million, valuing company at USD5 million, funded through IPO proceeds and internal accruals
items.quote: We completed this acquisition in April 2025, acquiring 51% stake for USD2.55 million, valuing the company at USD5 million.

items.statement: Remaining 49% stake purchase option linked to EBITDA multiple, timing and funding mix to be decided after integration
items.quote: No, it is an EBITDA multiple.

items.statement: No immediate acquisition plans for next quarter, focus on integration, solutioning and product building, but doors remain open
items.quote: We have not closed any doors. We are open and any strategic growth investments, we are always open to do it and take it. But ye s, at least, in the next quarter or so, we do not have any plans.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio remains low at 0.1x, reflecting conservative capital structure
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we remained pretty disciplined. Debt -to-equity ratio remains pretty low at 0 .1x, underlying a conservative, healthy capital structure.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations turned positive at INR3.8 crores driven by improved operational efficiency and tighter working capital management
items.quote: Most importantly, the cash flow from operations turned positive, coming in at INR3.8 crores, driven by improved operational efficiency and tighter working capital management.

items.statement: Water resource management now selectively bidding only on tenders with 60-70% upfront payment terms, avoiding old 40% upfront terms
items.quote: So we are very specific to participate in only tenders which are in the new norms now. So we do not want to participate the 40% of the contract value, which was the previous term.

items.statement: Added 63 new customers in FY25, total customer base grew from 115 to approximately 178
items.quote: We welcomed 63 new customers to Canarys family, many of them in new sectors and regions.

items.statement: Fortira brings 25+ large enterprise customers across banking, healthcare, telecom and pharma
items.quote: long -standing relationship with 25 plus large enterprise customers across banking, healthcare, telecom, and pharma

items.statement: Added over 100 professionals in FY25 across engineering, consulting, DevOps and AI roles, total 400+ professionals
items.quote: Between '24 and '25, we added over 100 professionals across engineering, consulting, multiple business units, be it, DevOps and the AI roles.

items.statement: Target to empower 25% of employees in AI, ML and data skills in FY26, 35% currently training at next level
items.quote: one of our top prioritie s for FY26 is to empower 25% of Canarians in AI, ML, and data skills, ensuring we build talent from within and lead responsibly in emerging technologies.

items.statement: Water resource management currently 35% of revenue, expected to reduce as percentage with technology solutions scaling
items.quote: Right now, the water management is at around 35% of the entire business. I think with the scale that we are looking at, this will reduce because the absolute number would still remain the same, but the percentage -wise, definitely it will reduce

items.statement: Fortira is pure IT solutions company, 100% impact on technology solutions vertical, no impact on water resource management
items.quote: Fortira Inc. is a pure IT solutions company. So the impact will be 100% on IT solutions vertical. There is not much impact on water resource management.

items.statement: More than 60% of order book comprises multi-year contracts (2-3 years), 40% short-term 6-month extendable contracts
items.quote: More than 60% is multi-year. We generally work on such kind of contracts. So 2 to 3 years is the contract size that we generally pick it up

items.statement: Management not providing direct guidance but indicates ~20% growth trajectory continuing with Fortira integration, bullish on FY26
items.quote: We have been growing around 20% and even if you continue at the same pace with Fortira Inc. coming in and Fort ira we anticipate to again grow not to decline this year.

items.statement: Order book execution mostly over next two years, minimal 15% spilling to third year, implies ~INR80 crores annual revenue visibility
items.quote: Most of the order book is for next two years and very minimum of this probably around 15% or so getting into the third year. But most of them is for next two years, this year and next year.

items.statement: Delivered 248 projects in FY25 across banking, insurance, manufacturing and government sectors
items.quote: We successfully delivered 248 projects during this year. These covered a wide range of industries, including banking, insurance, manufacturing, and government

items.statement: Revenue per employee has grown alongside headcount and solution expansion
items.quote: you can see that the number of resources have grown, number of solutions have grown, but at the same time even the revenue per employee has grown.

items.statement: Water resource management projects involve longer payment cycles, now pursuing selectively prioritizing speed, scale and commercial efficiency
items.quote: However, since these projects often involve longer payment cycles, we have now decided to pursue them more selectively, prioritizing speed, scale, and commercial efficiency.

items.statement: Government tenders shifting to new norms with 60-70% upfront payment, company only participating in new norm tenders
items.quote: You know, the government also changing and some of the latest tenders which they are floating has the new norms. So we are very specific to participate in only tenders which are in the new norms now.

items.statement: Management expects minimum 40% revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: We look at about 40% growth minimum to come this year , minimum 40%? Our numbers are higher, but minimum 40% is what we're looking at.

items.statement: Export order for concrete 3D printers to US announced on NSE; verbal orders from B2B platforms and Atal Tinkering Lab channel partners
items.quote: For the order book, we have already given numbers of, we are exporting some 3D printers to US, that is the concrete 3D printers, I have already announced on the NSE about the order book in that.

items.statement: Hardware gross margin 30-35%; prototyping higher; BRAHMA farm gross margin 70-80%; target revenue mix 70% hardware / 30% other categories in FY26
items.quote: So Deepakji, our dream is always to have the other part of the business having higher revenue, especially the entire BRAHMA category that we are creating. So we are focusing this year to be 70%-30%.

items.statement: BRAHMA 3D printing farm launching mid-July with 200-250 printers; target to scale to 1,000 and 5,000 printers
items.quote: Right now, everything is in place from the product portfolio for VINGLITS and also the products which BRAHMA will make and also the prototyping part of it. So like you said about industry partners, we are already working with a lot of corporates for their design and prototyping.

items.statement: BRAHMA farm daily production capacity ~2,000 pieces with 200-250 printers; plan to expand to 1,000-5,000 printers across India
items.quote: Where BRAHMA is a farm where we are looking at about 200 to 250 printers, my daily capacity of production is about 2,000 pieces.

items.statement: Launching VINGLITS premium 3D-printed toy brand (wild, aquatic, fantasy, reptiles) via quick commerce, online, and premium offline retailers like Hamleys
items.quote: VINGLITS is a make-in-India premium 3D printed toy brand that features product lines ranging from wild animals to aquatic animals, from fantasy figures to reptiles, and it will be available through online-channel distribution model, including we will also be on platforms like Zepto, Blinkit, QuickCommerce, and premium offline retailers like Ha mley's

items.statement: Atal Tinkering Labs expansion to 50,000 schools over 5 years; management targets 40% share (~20,000 schools) yielding ~INR100 cr revenue; B2C pull from student exposure
items.quote: I think the revenue -- I mean, even if we touch 40% of the schools that we are thinking out of 50,000, maybe 20,000 schools and average of INR50,000 revenue, we can -- it's a INR100 crores revenue that we see yet.

items.statement: Corporate prototyping orders: EV charger front parts (initial 100-200 units), pharma anatomical models (1,200 units); gifting exhibitions (GiftX, Delhi toy fair) to build pipeline
items.quote: we are working with a pharma company where they are making one anatomical model 1200 pieces for them

items.statement: Hired senior talent: National Sales Head for VINGLITS with 25 years toy industry experience; procurement from GM electrical; HR from senior company; building hierarchical team structure
items.quote: We right now recently recruited one of our, National Sales Head for the VINGLITS brand. He has 25 years of experience in the toy industry, one of the highest distribution network that he has.

items.statement: First-mover advantage in consumer 3D printing ecosystem; BRAHMA farm scale (2,000 pcs/day) vs home setups (12-20 pcs/day); own designs, packaging, distribution network as moat
items.quote: So Tanmayji, it is about the first mover advantage, first of all. Secondly, we are creating our own concept of products, which we are having our own premium packaging, our own distribution network.

items.statement: Consumer 3D printing organized market share 60-70% based on import data analysis; FY25 revenue INR48 cr (22% YoY), EBITDA INR7 cr (15% margin), PAT INR5.6 cr (11% YoY); 3-year CAGR: revenue 35%, EBITDA 83%, PAT 90%
items.quote: Today, we are happy to say that we command over 60% to 70% of the organized market share of consumer 3D printing in India.

items.statement: Government initiatives (Atal Tinkering Labs, digital manufacturing hubs, skill development) creating education sector opportunities; aligned with Make-in-India and Atmanirbhar Bharat
items.quote: The government's initiatives, such as Atal Tinkering labs or the digital manufacturing hubs or the skill development skills are creating significant opportunities for growth, especially in the education sector.

items.statement: Exporting concrete 3D printers to US; VINGLITS toys target export quality to boost exports and reduce imports
items.quote: We are exporting some 3D printers to US, that is the concrete 3D printers, I have already announced on the NSE about the order book in that.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with conservative balance sheet
items.quote: Additionally, we remain debt-free, maintaining a healthy and conservative balance sheet structure.

items.statement: Backward integration into PLA filament manufacturing at Bhiwandi plant gives control over pricing, quality, and supply chain efficiency
items.quote: We invested in backward integration by setting up our own PLA-based filament manufacturing plant in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra. This gave us complete control over our pricing, quality, and also the supply chain efficiency.

items.statement: Shift from third-party e-commerce (Amazon, Flipkart) to own website for better margins and direct customer interaction; adding quick commerce (Zepto, Blinkit) for VINGLITS
items.quote: E-commerce earlier used to focus on third-party e-commerce like Amazon, Flipkart. For the past one year, we have focused a lot on our own websites. Hence, you see B2C and also our website sales have increased a lot.

items.statement: Nine experience centers currently; target at least one in every state by FY27
items.quote: We currently operate about nine experience centers across India, and we aim to establish at least one in every state by the fiscal year 2027.

items.statement: Management targets 40% revenue growth for the current year.
items.quote: If my sales is increasing, this year we are looking at 40% growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined in H2 FY25 due to higher employee and admin expenses from senior hires and new experience centers.
items.quote: So sir, in this year, the EBITDA has been little reduced because like I answered earlier, we have recruited a lot of senior people from the industry.

items.statement: PAT margin is about 13%; management aims to maintain at least past margins but cannot give exact forward targets due to exchange rules.
items.quote: It is about 13% on the PAT. But if the revenue increases in a much better number, automatically the entire PAT numbers will change.

items.statement: B2C margins around 35%; B2B margins vary 10-14% depending on customer.
items.quote: B2C maybe 35%, maybe a B2B can be 10%, 14%. It depends on customer.

items.statement: BRAHMA 3D farm segment has very good margins.
items.quote: Sir, margins are very good in the entire BRAHMA as a segment for us.

items.statement: US clients have demanded 50,000 toy pieces per week, four times the planned 250-printer farm capacity of 12,000 pieces weekly.
items.quote: And the kind of demand that we got from those US clients, they wanted about 50,000 of pieces per week. So they already won four times in what we are already planning to start.

items.statement: Fixed assets will not increase much; investment mainly in 3D printing farm machines scaling with revenue.
items.quote: Sir, in the balance sheet, what I see is that our fixed assets will not be increasing much because the investment in the fixed assets is only the 3D printing farm, which will have a certain number of machines which are increasing as per the revenue increasing.

items.statement: VINGLITS brand launching July 4-7 at Delhi toy exhibition; 250 printers farm to be operational by mid-July for order fulfillment.
items.quote: From July 4 to 7 is when we are launching the brand in the toy exhibition in Delhi, which is the biggest exhibition in India. And for the order placement, right now, we are not taking any orders because we have just finished with the finalization of all the categories and also the packaging. So maybe from the mid of July, when the entire farm is into, you know, action, 250 printers is when we take

items.statement: A 1,000 printer farm can produce 60,000 toy pieces weekly; China has farms with 20,000 printers.
items.quote: Sir, a 1,000 printer farm can manufacture 20,000 3D printers as a farm, sir. Where a 1,000 printer farm can manufacture in a week about 60,000 pieces of toys. So you can imagine, sir, what we are looking at a 20,000 number farm.

items.statement: Inventory days increased because China shipment lead time rose from 45 to 70 days due to customs checks; company stocks 80% more inventory to support 40% growth.
items.quote: Right now, the product timeline when they export from China, those products, everything is being checked at the customs. So that wasted my 15 days more. And also, we are manufacturing and procuring in a high volume. So my timeline to get from China from 45 has become 70 days.

items.statement: Trade receivables stable at INR 4.8 crore vs INR 4 crore prior year; trade payables will increase with volumes.
items.quote: Like my trade receivables have been in 2023-24, it has been about INR4 crores. In this year, it was INR4.8 crores. So the trade receivables are not much.

items.statement: Company is debt-free, cash-rich, and plans to fund growth from internal accruals; no debt or equity raise planned currently.
items.quote: We are very positive about the cash that is there in hand, which will cater to all my needs, whether it is marketing, branding, fixed asset investment right now or any kind of variable cost.

items.statement: Future large investments may require debt/finance decision at that time.
items.quote: But if in the future, if you require any bigger investment that is to be done, that time we'll decide how the debt or the finance to be arranged.

items.statement: Toys import from China faces restrictions and high anti-dumping duties; not allowed in India.
items.quote: Sir, toys from China is not allowed. There are various restrictions. There are various requirements. There are other things. Maybe the other ways of importing may be there. But otherwise, toys are not allowed in India, sir. There are various restrictions to it. And there is higher, there is anti-dumping duty also, sir, very high.

items.statement: Government toy incentives exist but may be offset by higher labor/electricity costs in Category C/4 cities; evaluating middle path.
items.quote: When we were thinking of the government incentives, what we have realized is that maybe government incentives are in the category where you go to Category C cities and Category 4 cities. Although the incentives are higher, but the cost of labor, cost of electricity, and the other things that are required for a tech product like 3D printing technology, I think those costs will cover your incentive.

items.statement: Export strategy: start with Amazon Dubai and Amazon US for VINGLITS toys, then expand to retail/general trade.
items.quote: So what we are doing is that in the future coming in, I think the easier platform to export is maybe we are very strong on Amazon India, they have given us an opportunity to go into Amazon Dubai, and Amazon US. So maybe we look into these opportunities to come in to sell our toy brands first.

items.statement: Target revenue mix 70% hardware, 30% other (including BRAHMA); proportion may improve over time.
items.quote: Sir, we are looking at about 70% to 30%. 70% is hardware, 30% is the other category, which is higher revenue. And gradually, with time being and more number of volumes being increased, maybe the proportion will get more better.

items.statement: ~30% of hardware sold under own WOL3D brand (OEM); rest co-branded with partner brands.
items.quote: But there are various brands, maybe about 30% of the product we make under our own branding. So it's a completely OEM under the name of WOL3D.

items.statement: Consumables are inter-operable across brands; mostly own-branded consumables sold.
items.quote: So consumables are inter-used. It can be used in any branded 3D printer. Similarly, any other consumable can be used in my 3D pr inter also. So consumables, I feel in the long run, consumables obviously is going to be a very competitive market because it is easy to be a part of it because the investment is very less

items.statement: Discussions with Crossword, Hamleys, and other A-category stores for VINGLITS toy distribution.
items.quote: But we are in discussion with a lot of brands like Crossword. Crossword is there. Then we are discu ssing the Hamleys and various A category stores where we can have these toys

items.statement: Experience centers target 20x sales-to-cost monthly; Bangalore center does INR 80-90 lakh revenue on INR 4-5 lakh expense.
items.quote: So sir, what we are doing is that any office or any experience center that is opening, our target is to have a 20x sales on the cost which is being applied to those centers on a monthly basis. All the cities are performing great. We have good numbers coming in. Example, maybe Bangalore as a city, the revenue is about 80 to 90 lakhs that is coming in with an expense of about 4 to 5 lakhs.

items.statement: Claims 60-70% share of consumer 3D printing based on import data proportion.
items.quote: What we do is that we take the entire import data of the year and we see what is our proportion of the import data that has happened. So with that proportion, we get an idea we are about 60%-70% in this segment.

items.statement: All 3D printers imported (mainly from China); filaments manufactured in India; exploring Vietnam and other countries to diversify supply chain.
items.quote: All the products which are manufactured in the 3D printer segment is completely imported. 3D filament segment is ma nufactured in India in the factory. So maximum proportion of our business is imported because those machines cannot be made in

items.statement: No concrete timeline for supply chain diversification; will update stock exchange if any material development.
items.quote: These are nothing for right now of anything concrete. But if anything comes in, we will be updating on the stock exchange on immediate and priority basis.

items.statement: Consumables revenue grew 15% this year; overall numbers higher than last year.
items.quote: So consumables as a category also we are seeing good revenue. We have done 15% this year. Overall, the numbers have been higher than last year.

items.statement: No dead inventory in 7-8 years; older products find new buyers as technology adoption grows.
items.quote: So Parikshitji, we are very lucky and maybe the entire business model we have created in a way where we don't have any kind of dead inventory. All our inventories get sold.

items.statement: Recruited many senior industry people in last six months; employee benefit and admin expenses ~INR 75 lakh/month.
items.quote: So we have increased a lot of employee benefits that came into the expenses and also the admin expenses increased a lot because of the new product introduction and the new experience center introduction. So our expenses were about 75 lakhs per month has been there on the employee benefit expense and admin expenses.

items.statement: Divesting TaxTech ASP business to Sovos LLC via business transfer to subsidiary IRIS Logix; Sovos buying 100% of IRIS Logix shares
items.quote: The TaxTech business is being transferred through a business transfer arrangement into IRIS Logix, the subsidiary of IRIS. Sovos will be buying 100% of shares of IRIS Logix.

items.statement: Transaction value INR 151 crores; net asset value of transferred undertaking ~INR 6 crores as of 31st March
items.quote: if you see the stock exchange disclosure, so the net asset value of the business, the undertaking which is getting transferred is close to around INR 6 crores on the balance sheet as on 31st March.

items.statement: Long-term capital gains tax ~14% of overall transaction value; estimated capital gain ~INR 135 crores
items.quote: I think it will be close to around INR135 crores.

items.statement: Bulk of transaction money expected by August 2025; small holdback linked to license conditions; long-stop date October 1, 2025
items.quote: Now, the bulk of the transaction money should be coming in by August. There is a small holdback, which could come in after some time, and the long-stop date is October 1st, 2025.

items.statement: No earn-out model; holdback portion linked to license-related conditions
items.quote: There is no earned out model, but there is a holdback. There is a small holdback portion, which is linked to a couple of conditions.

items.statement: ~100 employees from GST business line moving to IRIS Logix/Sovos
items.quote: Roughly about 100 employees would move to the new IRIS Logix, I mean, to the new entity, IRIS Logix, which is the vehicle for this business.

items.statement: Malaysian e-invoicing business included in sale to Sovos
items.quote: Yes, so that the Malaysian e-invoicing business would eventually also go to this acquirer.

items.statement: IRIS Peridot app, MSME initiatives, and non-transferable GST/IRP licenses retained by parent company
items.quote: It is not. The IRIS, MSME, Peridot app is part of the parent company. This is not going to the acquirer.

items.statement: Remaining GST pipeline revenue ~INR 1.2 crores stays with IRIS
items.quote: Yes. So, the remaining revenue from the GST part of the business, which is essentially pipeline, which is the pipeline to GSTN would be about INR1.2 crores.

items.statement: Medium-term aspiration to reach INR 500 crores revenue in 4-5 years from current ~INR 128-130 crores
items.quote: Broadly, I would say our next medium-term target is to be INR500 crores company. We are about INR128 crores, INR130 crores. So, this is a medium-term target, which we have set for ourselves to be a INR500 crores company.

items.statement: No formal guidance given on growth and margin trajectory despite fund availability
items.quote: I'm afraid that I can't give any guidance. We said that whatever we had to say in terms of the trajectory, we have to hit and how do we plan to move on that trajectory.

items.statement: Aggressive investment planned in enterprise SaaS (IRIS CARBON), sales & marketing, talent, and product development; mostly OPEX
items.quote: We'll be setting aside a pool of money to bring in solid talent, both within specific business lines and leadership positions, cutting across business lines. And these are people who should integrate well in IRIS and work with our current talent pool to drive the next level of growth.

items.statement: TaxTech segment had ~INR 3 crores EBITDA loss on ~INR 16.5 crores revenue in FY25; removal from Q2 FY26 onwards
items.quote: In fact, we are running close to a INR3 crores loss in the segment reporting level in the TaxTech business. So of course, that is now going to the new entity.

items.statement: EBITDA margins may face temporary pressure from aggressive OPEX spending on sales-led growth despite loss-making segment exit
items.quote: There is a bit of a trade-off between the profits you get from the SupTech business versus the kind of investments you need to make in the enterprise SaaS business. Enterprise SaaS business investments could be at a higher pace in the initial years compared to the SupTech business growth, and therefore the higher EBITDA coming from there.

items.statement: No need to raise further capital (dilutive or PE) as deal proceeds sufficient for growth plans
items.quote: But we don't see any need for raising more money at this point of time. Our sense is whatever we are getting through this deal should stand us in good stead as we look at growing to our next target.

items.statement: Stronger balance sheet targeted to attract right partners; no specific debt reduction or refinancing mentioned
items.quote: Finally, we need a deep war chest to make this happen, and our balance sheet needs to be stronger so that we can attract the right partners.

items.statement: Cross-sell opportunities with Sovos for existing GST customers; no impact on IRIS DataTech lending enablement business
items.quote: So, I don't see there will be any problems in terms of working with our existing GST customers and offering them more from the IRIS main parent company suite.

items.statement: Strategic shift from product-led to sales-led growth; focus on value-led and productivity-led sales to medium/large enterprises; IRIS CARBON for CFO/CSO office
items.quote: We are now shifting our DNA again for a growth move from product-led growth to sales-led growth. This means much stronger investments in sales and marketing, hiring more folks in our target geographies as well.

items.statement: Global RegTech competitors have substantially higher outlay for sales, marketing, product development; need bigger balance sheet to compete
items.quote: If you look at our global competitors in the RegTech business, they do have a substantially higher outlay, deep pockets for sales and marketing, and product development expenses.

items.statement: Morale high among transferring GST team; sees global expansion opportunity with Sovos in APAC
items.quote: I think the morale is pretty high. So, if I can say, how's the josh? Josh is very high, because it gives the GST team a good opportunity to expand their wings and the landscape goes beyond India because Sovos being a large leader in the space allows us this opportunity to take our solutions globally, especially in the APAC level.

items.statement: Promoter holding stable in absolute terms; quarter-on-quarter percentage changes due to ESOPs and Swaminathan stake moving to Deepta
items.quote: I don't think there is any constant decrease in the promoter holding quarter-on-quarter. There were some ESOPs we had given. So that might have led to some dilution as far as promoter percentage holding is concerned. In terms of absolute numbers, I don't think there has been any reduction.

items.statement: ESG reporting demand gradual pickup from this year; European mandate coverage paced out but voluntary adoption continues
items.quote: So, I think our solutions are anyway getting out there in the market, and we feel gradual pickup. That's what I would say. There's definitely going to be gradual pickup from this year onwards.

items.statement: AGM scheduled July 26 for shareholder approval of business transfer as material related party transaction
items.quote: We are holding an AGM on July 26th to get shareholder approval of the business transfer, since it's a material related party transaction.

items.statement: Amazon discontinued refurbished sales in Feb-Mar 2025, removing ~60% of revenue; first 10 months grew 25% YoY before disruption
items.quote: Amazon as a marketplace, took a decision to not sell any refurbished products across any categories from February-March 2025. And as Amazon was contributing almost 60% of our revenues , i t had a significant impact on our revenue and profitability

items.statement: Target monthly revenue run rate of Rs 5-5.25 Cr to reach break-even; currently at Rs 3-3.5 Cr run rate
items.quote: I think if we reach back to you know, like 5 plus number, we should be at a break- even level as per our internal like measures that we are taking right. Ashish Nirmal 5 Vishesh Handa 5 to 5.25 top line- we should be at a break-even level as such

items.statement: Expect to reach prior peak monthly revenue run rate by end of FY26; PAT recovery likely in FY27
items.quote: So from the peak, I would say we, our other Channel revenue was around 35%, which has already grown by almost like 100% now, but this is the year we are looking at as a year of consolidation and we are strongly striving towards making sure that by the end of the year we are already at the revenue run rate which was the peak last year.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped to ~25% in H2 due to Rs 3.5-3.7 Cr Amazon arbitration markdown, Rs 2.5 Cr aging inventory markdown, and a low-margin trading deal; underlying margin 37-38%
items.quote: If we remove these, I think we are around 37% to 40% is the sweet spot that we are still like seeing. But yes, I mean around 3.6 to 3.7 Cr. of arbitration like, which is still in arbitration.

items.statement: Website channel BTL cost 13-14% vs Amazon's 11-12%; adding 4-5% ATL spend makes total 17-19% vs Amazon's 11-12%
items.quote: just on performance marketing , our spend levels, including performance marketing, our tele sales team, returns and logistics- We are around 13% to 14%. Anshul Jain Okay. Vishesh Handa That's our BTL. I want to also call out that we are now spending 4% to 5% of our top line on ATL

items.statement: B2B/enterprise segment grew from ~1% to 40% of revenue in 3 months; signed 88+ new clients including 4 deals >Rs 1 Cr each (large NBFC, media house)
items.quote: We have just in span of a quarter signed more than 88 new clients now, out of that, 4 are very large deals with each deal more than 1 Cr. One of which is the one of the largest NBFCs in India.

items.statement: Education vertical: closed 2 engineering college deals and 5 school deals in Karnataka; strong pipeline building
items.quote: We have already closed 2 large deals with engineering colleges and 5 with schools just in around Karnataka as such. We have built a strong pipeline in that regard.

items.statement: Distribution/modern trade: 35+ large format stores (Poorvika), distributors in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, Karnataka multi-chain; sales expected from July

items.quote: Despite the stable overall deposit levels, CASA ratio has witnessed a decline on a sequential basis from 47.01% to 45.71%. This reduction has been driven primarily by migration of CASA balances to term deposits for locking in of higher yields prior to the deposit interest rate cut.

items.statement: CRAR 15.98%, CET-1 12.69% (excl. Q1 profits adding 48 bps)
items.quote: CRAR has been recorded at 15.98% with CET-1 at 12.69%. This is without reckoning the net profits for Q1 which has an incremental impact of 48 bps.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Pahalgam incident) impacted tourism and allied sectors; some SMA-2 creep but manageable via restructuring
items.quote: As I mentioned, the slippages have been less than 1%. And the credit cost will remain low compared to other banks as it has been for this Bank for the past several quarters. First of all, there is no major large corporate account which is under any kind of stress at the moment.

items.statement: One-time impairment provision INR87 crores for J&K Grameen Bank investment due to RRB amalgamation under 'One State, One RRB'
items.quote: Also, I would like to emphasize here that in Q1, our profitability has been impacted by a one-time impairment provision of INR87 crores related to our investment in J&K Grameen Bank necessitated due to erosion of the equity value on account of amalgamation of J&K Grameen Bank and Ellaquai Dehati Bank into a single RRB under our sponsorship in line with the directives issued by the Government of In

items.statement: Excluding one-time provision, net profit growth would be upwards of 30% YoY
items.quote: Excluding this one-time provision, our net profit growth would be upwards of 30% YoY.

items.statement: Targeting 50:50 portfolio split between J&K and rest of India (currently 70:30)
items.quote: My credit growth will come 50% from Jammu and Kashmir region and 50% from rest of India. This is for this financial year. Going forward, my portfolio I want the portfolio to be 50:50. At the moment, it is 70:30.

items.statement: Corporate lending competitive; clients demand rates bank cannot always match; focus on retail for sustainable margins
items.quote: And you know that generally, the clients that we look at, they are very tough on the margins, they demand rates which sometimes banks like us we are not able to provide.
